To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
repeated measurements of endothelial function using EndoPAT show moderate reliability on the same day and substantial on day to day measurements.
repeated measurements of fRHi show moderate reliability on the same day and substantial reliability on the next day in patients with acute ischemic stroke.
repeated measurements of fRhi in stroke patients show substantial reliability on day‐to‐day and fair to moderate reliability on same‐day measurements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a new, noninvasive method of measuring endothelial function in stroke patients.
the reliability of the EndoPAT device in the context of stroke patients and healthy controls.
the reliability of repeated measurements of RHI in acute stroke patients and in healthy subjects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
repeated measurements of fRHi in healthy subjects and stroke patients show substantial reliability.
repeated measurements of fRhi show a fair reliability in stroke patients and a moderate reliability in healthy subjects.
repeated measurements of EF using the EndoPAT2000 are reliable in healthy volunteers and in stroke patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the EndoPAT technology is a reliable method to measure endothelial function in stroke patients, and the Framingham RHI is a more reliable outcome measure than the RHI and ln(RHI) in this patient cohort.
repeated measurement of EF using EndoPAT200 in stroke patients and healthy subjects is reliable, but not highly reliable.
the EndoPAT device can be used in acute stroke patients for the assessment of endothelial function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EndoPAT is reliable enough to be used in clinical studies to measure drug effects.
day-to-day repeated measurement of fRHI may be a useful tool in clinical studies of EF in stroke patients.
day-to-day reliability of EF measurement in healthy subjects and stroke patients is substantial.
